opportunities.timing: 3rd Saturdays, 3:00-5:00 PM (dates are on their calendar)
requirements: The hillside can be steep and uneven
Wear a sunhat and bring layers
signupSteps: Open the RSVP and volunteer waiver form linked from Test Plot's event calendar
Submit the form for an upcoming Ohlone Hillside workday
At the Lawrence Hall of Science main entrance, say you are volunteering at the hillside
whatYoullDo: Join a community workday led by UC Berkeley student fellows
Water and weed around native plants
Borrow gloves and tools if you need them
opportunities.impactLine: Steady hands help a young native-plant plot make it through each season.
opportunities.impactDone: You just gave one Berkeley hillside two hours of practical care.

opportunities.title: Build and repair Berkeley paths
opportunities.blurb: Join a two-hour weekday crew or a monthly Saturday crew caring for Berkeley's public paths.
opportunities.description: Hands-on path-building crews where senior path builders train volunteers to replace damaged treads, improve stormwater drainage, and plan handrails.
opportunities.timing: Mondays and Wednesdays, 9:00-11:00 AM; one Saturday each month, 9:00 AM-12:00 PM
requirements: Fill out the path-building volunteer form
signupSteps: Open the path-building signup linked on the Berkeley Path Wanderers homepage
Add your contact details and availability (weekday, monthly Saturday, or occasional), then submit
whatYoullDo: Remove and replace damaged treads
Improve stormwater drainage
Help plan handrails
opportunities.impactLine: Careful repairs keep Berkeley's public paths safer and easier to use.
opportunities.impactDone: You just gave a public path a session of repair work.

opportunities.org: City of Berkeley Parks and Recreation
opportunities.title: Clean the Berkeley waterfront
opportunities.blurb: Drop in on a third Saturday morning to pick up litter along the Berkeley shoreline.
opportunities.description: A two-hour shoreline cleanup starting at Shorebird Park Nature Center, with supplies, including gloves and buckets, provided.
opportunities.locationLabel: Shorebird Park Nature Center, 160 University Avenue
requirements: Groups of 5 or more should RSVP in advance
Under 15 must come with an adult
Ages 15-17: parent or guardian signs waiver on-site
signupSteps: Check the City page for the next third-Saturday cleanup
Come to Shorebird Park Nature Center between 9:00 and 11:00 AM
Groups of 5 or more should email the Nature Center before coming
whatYoullDo: Check in at the Nature Center
Collect provided cleanup gear
Pick up litter along the waterfront
opportunities.impactLine: A regular cleanup keeps plastic and other litter from settling into the Bay.
opportunities.impactDone: You just helped leave part of Berkeley's shoreline cleaner.

opportunities.title: Take an on-call meal delivery shift
opportunities.blurb: Join the on-call list for a weekday morning packing or delivery shift in Berkeley.
opportunities.description: A one-hour Meals on Wheels shift that starts in West Berkeley after an application and background check.
opportunities.locationLabel: Meals on Wheels Office, 1925 Ninth Street
opportunities.timing: On-call Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday mornings
requirements: Fill out a volunteer application form
18+ to volunteer alone; volunteers under 18 need adult supervision
Drivers need a valid license, vehicle, and current auto insurance
signupSteps: Email MealsOnWheels@BerkeleyCA.gov and ask to join the on-call list
Complete the volunteer application and background check
Accept an available packing or delivery shift when the team contacts you
whatYoullDo: Start your shift at the West Berkeley office
Pack meals or deliver them to homebound seniors
opportunities.impactLine: An on-call volunteer helps the meal route stay covered when the regular crew is short.
opportunities.impactDone: You just helped one morning of Berkeley meal deliveries stay on track.

opportunities.title: Help at a La Peña event
opportunities.blurb: Help with onsite event support at La Peña events in Berkeley, and get free entry to the event you volunteer at.
opportunities.description: Volunteer for events at La Peña Cultural Center through its volunteer form. The form lists onsite event support, including an option with public interaction, and asks when you are available.
opportunities.locationLabel: La Peña Cultural Center, 3105 Shattuck Avenue
signupSteps: Open La Peña's volunteer form
Choose onsite event support and share your availability
Say why you want to volunteer and submit the form
whatYoullDo: Help with onsite event support
Choose an option with public interaction, if you like
opportunities.impactLine: An extra set of hands helps a busy community event feel organized and welcoming.
opportunities.impactDone: You just helped one La Peña event run more smoothly.

opportunities.title: Help with an art event or installation
opportunities.blurb: Apply to be on call for an event, exhibition installation, or cleanup day at Berkeley Art Center.
opportunities.description: A bimonthly or quarterly on-call shift helping Berkeley Art Center with events, gallery installations, facility upkeep, or community cleanup days.
opportunities.timing: On-call for bimonthly or quarterly projects
requirements: Fill out the volunteer application form
Facility upkeep: lift 50 pounds, climb a ladder
Installation: comfortable with hand tools and ladders
signupSteps: Fill out the general volunteer application form on Berkeley Art Center's volunteer page
Receive your volunteer application from the gallery
whatYoullDo: Help set up an event, install art, or care for the grounds
opportunities.impactLine: On-call help gives a small gallery more hands for the busy work around exhibitions and events.
opportunities.impactDone: You just helped Berkeley Art Center prepare one event, exhibition, or shared space.

opportunities.title: Help at the Berkeley Farmers’ Market
opportunities.blurb: Help at the Berkeley Farmers’ Market with booth set-up and take-down or merchandise sales.
opportunities.description: A Berkeley Farmers’ Market role through the Ecology Center’s volunteer application, where you share your availability and how long you can help.
opportunities.timing: Shift lengths vary — you share your availability when you apply
requirements: Fill in the required application fields
Sign the volunteer agreement and release
signupSteps: Open the Ecology Center volunteer application
Choose Berkeley Farmers' Market and enter your availability
Add an emergency contact and sign the volunteer agreement
whatYoullDo: Help set up and take down the booth
Help with merchandise sales
opportunities.impactLine: A staffed market booth helps neighbors use food-access programs and find their way around the market.
opportunities.impactDone: You just helped one market stay useful and welcoming.

organizations.name: Be My Eyes
organizations.blurb: Connects volunteers by smartphone with people who need help checking or reading something visual. A few clear words can help someone finish the small task in front of them.

organizations.name: Cake4Kids
organizations.blurb: Turns home baking into birthday care for kids in foster care. Volunteers claim a cake request, bake at home, and drop it off in San Francisco.

organizations.name: Cardz for Kidz
organizations.blurb: Collects warm cards made at home for hospitalized kids. Volunteers keep the message simple and kind, then mail the card to Cardz for Kidz.

organizations.name: Catchafire
organizations.blurb: Matches volunteers with nonprofits that need focused professional help. A clear hour of expertise can remove a real roadblock for a small nonprofit team.

organizations.name: CareerVillage
organizations.blurb: Crowdsources career advice from professionals so students can get answers about many career paths. Volunteers answer questions online from the experience they already have.

organizations.name: Civic Joy Fund
organizations.blurb: Brings San Franciscans together for neighborhood cleanups, park care, and other practical ways to tend shared public spaces. Its public events make it easy to choose a place, meet a local crew, and leave one small part of the city better cared for.

organizations.name: Curry Senior Center
organizations.blurb: Serves seniors in the Tenderloin with daily meals, community, and health support. Volunteers help serve breakfast and lunch so older neighbors can share a warm meal together.

organizations.name: Distributed Proofreaders
organizations.blurb: Turns careful proofreading into cleaner public-domain books. Volunteers compare one scanned page with its text and fix small errors for Project Gutenberg.

organizations.name: Friends of the Urban Forest
organizations.blurb: Brings neighbors together for Saturday street-tree plantings around San Francisco. A morning of planting and cleanup can grow into years of shade.

organizations.name: GLIDE
organizations.blurb: Offers hands-on Tenderloin roles, from serving daily free meals to walking as a community ambassador. Volunteers help guests with basic care and help the block feel more attended to.

organizations.name: Golden Gate Bird Alliance
organizations.blurb: Cares for bird habitat in the middle of the city. Volunteers check in at North Lake, help with habitat work, and return tools at the end of the shift.

organizations.name: Gardens of Golden Gate Park
organizations.blurb: Cares for the Botanical Garden, Conservatory of Flowers, and Japanese Tea Garden. Volunteers join departments such as the nursery, horticulture, library reception, and event support after an application and orientation.

organizations.name: Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy
organizations.blurb: Offers practical Presidio stewardship, from caring for the urban forest to growing native plants at the nursery. Volunteers help with steady outdoor work that supports healthier habitat.

organizations.name: Habitat for Humanity Greater San Francisco
organizations.blurb: Builds and preserves affordable homes across San Francisco and the Peninsula. Volunteers help prepare materials and repair homes, and no construction experience is necessary.

organizations.name: IRS VITA
organizations.blurb: Helps neighbors file taxes for free after volunteers complete IRS certification. The work can happen at San Francisco sites or from home during tax season.

organizations.name: Lasagna Love
organizations.blurb: Matches volunteers with nearby families for one homemade lasagna. Volunteers accept a match, cook at home, and deliver the meal as arranged.

organizations.name: LibriVox
organizations.blurb: Makes free public-domain audiobooks through volunteer recordings. Volunteers register on the forum, claim chapters or short works, and record with basic software.

organizations.name: Library of Congress (By the People)
organizations.blurb: Makes Library of Congress documents easier to search and discover from home. Volunteers transcribe pages, review other transcriptions, and help complete public records.

organizations.name: Litquake
organizations.blurb: Brings readers and writers together at literary events across San Francisco. Volunteers greet guests, help at the box office, and support book signings during the fall festival and occasional year-round events.

organizations.name: Little Brothers - Friends of the Elderly
organizations.blurb: Creates steady company for older neighbors through calls, visits, and nearby strolls. Volunteers complete orientation, coordinate a rhythm, and offer a friendly check-in or shared walk.

organizations.name: MapSwipe
organizations.blurb: Uses volunteer swipes to improve geospatial data projects around the world. Volunteers use the web or mobile app to identify features, compare imagery, or validate map data.

organizations.name: Meals on Wheels SF
organizations.blurb: Gets meals to homebound seniors through weekday delivery routes. Volunteers pick up meals, deliver to seniors at home, and report any route notes.

organizations.name: Missing Maps
organizations.blurb: Turns from-home mapping into useful detail for disaster relief. Volunteers pick a mapping task, trace visible features, and save edits that can help response teams navigate with less guesswork.

organizations.name: New Conservatory Theatre Center
organizations.blurb: Produces theatre for queer and allied communities in Civic Center. Volunteer ushers help the front-of-house team welcome audiences and settle the room before a performance.

organizations.name: Muttville Senior Dog Rescue
organizations.blurb: Supports senior dogs through in-person care at HQ and from-home adoption bio writing. Volunteers help older dogs feel cared for, seen, and ready for the next step.

organizations.name: Nature in the City
organizations.blurb: Cares for butterfly habitat around San Francisco. Volunteers meet at the habitat site and help with restoration.

organizations.name: Openhouse
organizations.blurb: Connects volunteers with LGBTQ+ elders through friendly visits and calls. Warm, reliable company helps elders feel remembered by their community.

organizations.name: Presidio Habitat Stewards
organizations.blurb: Tends native habitat in the Presidio through calendar-listed outdoor events. Volunteers meet the habitat stewards and care for native habitat.

organizations.name: Project Open Hand
organizations.blurb: Prepares meals for sick and elderly neighbors in its San Francisco kitchen. Volunteers help prep, portion, package, and label meals.

organizations.name: Randall Museum
organizations.blurb: Keeps the native pollinator garden at Randall Museum cared for and tidy. Volunteers check in at the museum and help tend pollinator plants in Corona Heights.

organizations.name: Rocket Dog Rescue
organizations.blurb: Supports rescue dogs through adoption-event help and flexible dog walking. Volunteers help dogs stay comfortable, support the adoption team, or give a rescue dog a calmer stretch of day.

organizations.name: San Francisco SPCA
organizations.blurb: Helps shelter animals through calm cat socializing and foster care at home. Volunteers complete the sign-up steps, coordinate with the shelter, and follow shelter guidance.

organizations.name: San Francisco Bicycle Coalition
organizations.blurb: Promotes the bicycle for everyday transportation in San Francisco. Volunteers wrench at community repair nights, staff tables at neighborhood events, and pitch in on office tasks at the monthly volunteer night.

organizations.name: San Francisco Fleet Week Association
organizations.blurb: Runs San Francisco Fleet Week and its public air shows, ship tours, and waterfront events. Volunteers help guests find their way through the large October program.

organizations.name: San Francisco Village
organizations.blurb: Connects volunteers with older neighbors for flexible practical help around San Francisco. A small errand or task can keep a neighbor's day from getting stuck.

organizations.name: Shanti Project
organizations.blurb: Runs PAWS (Pets Are Wonderful Support) for older adults and adults with illnesses and disabilities who need help caring for their companion animals. Volunteers walk dogs, care for cats in the home, foster, and drive pets to vet appointments.

organizations.name: Save The Bay
organizations.blurb: Restores Bay shoreline habitat through guided calendar-listed shifts. Volunteers check in with the team and help restore habitat.

organizations.name: SF Animal Care & Control
organizations.blurb: Brings volunteers into flexible shelter outreach events after orientation. The work helps more animals and neighbors find the right shelter support.

organizations.name: SF Civic Tech
organizations.blurb: Welcomes people into Wednesday civic project hack nights, with no tech skills required. Volunteers pick a project table and help with a first useful task.

organizations.name: SF Public Library
organizations.blurb: Supports adult learners through Project Read tutoring at the Main Library or branches. Volunteers complete tutor training and practice reading with an adult learner each week.

organizations.name: SF Recreation & Parks
organizations.blurb: Offers neighborhood park and habitat workdays around San Francisco. Volunteers check in at the park, help with the day's outdoor tasks, and return tools before leaving.

organizations.name: Friends of the San Francisco Public Library
organizations.blurb: Raises funds and advocates for the San Francisco Public Library. Volunteers staff the Friends Bookstore at the Main Library, prepare online sales, and process book donations.

organizations.name: La Cocina
organizations.blurb: Helps low-income and immigrant women build formal food businesses. Volunteers work one-on-one with entrepreneurs as skilled technical assistance providers and mentors.

organizations.name: SF Public Works
organizations.blurb: Cares for San Francisco streets, trees, gardens, and public spaces. Its volunteer events pair neighbors with staff and community groups for hands-on greening, cleanup, and neighborhood beautification work.

organizations.name: SF-Marin Food Bank
organizations.blurb: Gets groceries and meals closer to San Francisco neighbors. Volunteers sort produce, pack food for distribution, deliver groceries, and welcome shoppers at Community Markets.

organizations.name: Smithsonian Transcription Center
organizations.blurb: Turns historical pages into searchable text from home. Volunteers choose a page, type what they can read, and submit it for review.

organizations.name: St. Anthony's
organizations.blurb: Offers practical Tenderloin shifts across lunch service, clothing, and basic tech help. Volunteers serve guests, sort useful items, or sit with someone working through a next step.

organizations.name: Surfrider SF
organizations.blurb: Organizes Sunday morning Ocean Beach cleanups. Volunteers meet the cleanup group and pick up litter along the sand.

organizations.name: Sutro Stewards
organizations.blurb: Restores Mount Sutro trails during first-and-third Saturday morning shifts. Volunteers check in with the crew, help with trail work, and wrap up with lunch after the shift.

organizations.name: Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation
organizations.blurb: Provides affordable homes and neighborhood health programs in the Tenderloin and nearby communities. Its public gardens welcome a few volunteers at a time during weekly open hours.

organizations.name: Upwardly Global
organizations.blurb: Helps immigrants and refugees rebuild professional careers in the United States. Volunteers share workplace knowledge through from-home interviews, profile reviews, and career conversations.

organizations.name: Taproot Plus
organizations.blurb: Connects volunteers with nonprofits that need one focused hour of professional expertise. Volunteers choose a consultation and give clear, practical help.

organizations.name: Team Rubicon
organizations.blurb: Starts veterans and civilians on a flexible Bay Area service crew path. Volunteers sign up, complete a short intro training, and join organized service work.

organizations.name: Foster Love
organizations.blurb: Turns at-home Sweet Cases projects into practical care for kids in foster care. Volunteers use Foster Love instructions for individual at-home projects.

organizations.name: Translators Without Borders
organizations.blurb: Uses language fluency to help humanitarian information reach more people. Volunteers create a translator profile, review available work, and translate a bounded task.

organizations.name: Alemany Farm
organizations.blurb: Welcomes volunteers to community farm workdays at the Alemany Farm site. Volunteers register, check in, and help with practical farm tasks like planting, weeding, mulching, and harvest work.

organizations.name: City Hope SF
organizations.blurb: Runs a Tenderloin community center with meals, cafe time, gathering space, and neighborhood care. Volunteers pick posted shifts through the City Hope volunteer portal.

organizations.name: Florence Fang Community Farm
organizations.blurb: Grows food and community at a Bayview-Hunters Point farm. Saturday drop-in volunteers help with hands-on farm work during public community farm hours.

organizations.name: Garden for the Environment
organizations.blurb: Maintains a public organic teaching garden in the Inner Sunset. Volunteers book Wednesday or Saturday garden days and help with guided outdoor work.

organizations.name: Martin de Porres House of Hospitality
organizations.blurb: Serves free lunch six days a week through an all-volunteer house of hospitality. Individual volunteers can walk in during the volunteer window and help prepare, serve, or clean up.

organizations.name: Project Homeless Connect
organizations.blurb: Connects unhoused San Franciscans with practical support through service events, outreach, hygiene kits, and office help. Volunteers choose posted roles through VolunteerHub.

organizations.name: Refuse Refuse SF
organizations.blurb: Organizes public neighborhood cleanups across San Francisco. Volunteers choose a cleanup from the calendar, meet the local crew, and help pick up litter.

organizations.name: SF Food Not Bombs
organizations.blurb: Cooks and shares free vegan meals in San Francisco through volunteer-run weekly crews. New volunteers contact the crew for the day they want and then help cook, share, or clean up.

organizations.name: The Food Pantry
organizations.blurb: Runs a volunteer-powered Saturday food pantry at St. Gregory of Nyssa. New volunteers contact the pantry first, then help set up, share groceries, and close down.

organizations.name: CodePath
organizations.blurb: Connects college computer science students with short from-home career sessions. Volunteers review a resume, run a practice interview, or share focused career guidance.

organizations.name: National AIDS Memorial
organizations.blurb: Cares for the National AIDS Memorial Grove in Golden Gate Park. Community workdays bring volunteers together to tend plants, paths, and memorial features.

organizations.name: The Marsh
organizations.blurb: Presents new performance work at its Valencia Street theatre. Volunteers choose dated front-of-house shifts and help audiences settle in before a show.

organizations.name: Safe & Sound
organizations.blurb: Supports San Francisco families through practical services and parent support. Small volunteer groups prepare and package Monday dinners that staff distribute to parents and children.

organizations.name: Haight Ashbury Food Program
organizations.blurb: Runs a Saturday grocery pantry from the Waller Center in Haight-Ashbury. Volunteers receive and sort food, set up shopping stations, and help close the pantry after distribution.

organizations.name: Kimochi
organizations.blurb: Serves older adults through meals, activities, transportation, and residential support. One-time volunteers can help with weekday lunch service without the health paperwork required for ongoing facility roles.

organizations.name: Zooniverse
organizations.blurb: Turns small from-home observations into help for real research projects. Volunteers choose a project, review one image or item, and mark what they observe.

organizations.name: Alameda County Community Food Bank
organizations.blurb: Runs an Oakland warehouse that supplies food programs across Alameda County. Volunteers sort produce, pack emergency food boxes, and help keep grocery distribution moving.

organizations.name: Community Kitchens
organizations.blurb: Prepares meals for Oakland neighbors from a central kitchen near Telegraph Avenue. Volunteers prep ingredients, make sandwiches and wraps, and package meals for distribution.

organizations.name: Friends of the Gardens at Lake Merritt
organizations.blurb: Helps care for the public Gardens at Lake Merritt through recurring volunteer workdays. Newcomers can join a Friday or Saturday crew with tools available.

organizations.name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
organizations.blurb: Builds and preserves affordable homes across the East Bay and South Bay. Its Oakland ReStore keeps donated home goods in use and helps fund the housing work.

organizations.name: Lake Merritt Institute
organizations.blurb: Cares for Lake Merritt through regular public cleanups and water stewardship. Newcomers can join a weekday or weekend crew with supplies and safety guidance provided.

organizations.name: Homies Empowerment
organizations.blurb: Runs community food and youth programs rooted in East Oakland. Volunteers help grow food at the Freedom Farm and sort, pack, and distribute free groceries at the Freedom Store.

organizations.name: Oakland First Fridays
organizations.blurb: Runs Oakland's monthly Telegraph Avenue street festival. Event volunteers help the public program stay organized from setup through wrap-up.

organizations.name: St. Vincent de Paul of Alameda County
organizations.blurb: Runs a free dining room and community services from its West Oakland campus. Volunteers help prepare and serve meals alongside staff.

organizations.name: Berkeley Art Center
organizations.blurb: Runs a contemporary art gallery in Live Oak Park. On-call volunteers help with events, exhibition installations, facility care, and community cleanup days.

organizations.name: Berkeley Meals on Wheels
organizations.blurb: Packs and delivers weekday meals for homebound Berkeley seniors. Volunteers can join the on-call list when a weekly commitment does not fit.

organizations.name: Berkeley Path Wanderers Association
organizations.blurb: Builds, repairs, and maintains Berkeley's network of public paths and stairways. Experienced crew members teach newcomers how to work safely with the team.

organizations.name: Berkeley Food Network
organizations.blurb: Runs neighborhood pantries, home delivery, and food recovery from its West Berkeley warehouse. Volunteers help keep groceries sorted, stocked, and ready for pickup.

organizations.name: Ecology Center
organizations.blurb: Runs Berkeley farmers’ markets and other environmental programs. Market volunteers help with booths, merchandise, setup, and seasonal events.

organizations.name: Insight Housing
organizations.blurb: Provides meals, shelter, housing, and support in Berkeley. Its weekday Community Meal at the Hope Center is open to neighbors experiencing food insecurity.

organizations.name: City of Berkeley Parks and Recreation
organizations.blurb: Coordinates public-space, habitat, and community-event volunteering across Berkeley. Its third-Saturday shoreline cleanup is open to drop-in volunteers.

organizations.name: La Peña Cultural Center
organizations.blurb: Hosts music, dance, and community events in South Berkeley. Volunteers help with individual events in public-facing or behind-the-scenes roles.

organizations.name: Test Plot
organizations.blurb: Builds small native-plant plots as places for hands-on learning and habitat care. Berkeley volunteers tend the Ohlone Hillside plot at Lawrence Hall of Science.
